why.label: How was this worked out?
why.qtyDefault: The quantity listed in the wishlist.
why.local: Bought in Mongolia, or the quote is already delivered with VAT included — so the price is used as it is. No shipping, customs duty or VAT is added.
why.import: Imported. Each step is charged on everything before it:
why.wfLanded: Cost at the lodge, per unit
why.shipping: Freight to Ulaanbaatar as a share of the price. About 4% for normal goods by truck or container (mostly from China). About 12.5% for bulky or dangerous goods: snowmobiles, lithium batteries, large doors and fuel tanks. The trip on from UB to Dadal is in the countryside premium.
why.fx: Used to turn dollar prices into tögrög. ₮3,650 is the planning rate used across the 2027 budget. Prices quoted in tögrög (the jet boat and the telecom station) don't change with it.
why.duty: Mongolia's standard customs duty is 5%. It is charged on the price plus shipping, and only for items marked Imported.
why.vat: Mongolian VAT is 10%. For imports it is paid at the border, on the price + shipping + customs duty. Local prices already include VAT, so it isn't added again.
why.guests: Expected guest-nights in 2027, from the 2027 projection. Only used for the 'share of guests' check — it doesn't change any money figure.
why.scenario: Three sets of sales numbers. Base is our central estimate. Conservative: prices about 15% lower, about 40% fewer sales per day and a 10–15% shorter season; running costs unchanged. Aggressive: prices about 20% higher and about 40% more sales; running costs about 15% higher because of the extra use. The cost of buying things doesn't change between scenarios. The site opens on Conservative.
why.salesNote: The figures above are for Base; Conservative and Aggressive move them as explained on the Assumptions page.
why.perDay: Average number sold on each operating day, across all units together. 0.5 means one sale every other day.
why.days: Days a year it can actually run, after season and weather.
why.opex: Yearly cost to keep it running: fuel or electricity, servicing, staff time, insurance, storage.
why.payback: {capex} investment ÷ {net} net revenue a year = {y} years
why.paybackLoss: Running costs are higher than sales, so it never pays back on these numbers.
why.capexShare: Only {p} of this item's cost is counted here — the rest of the building stores other equipment.
why.attach: {units} sales a year ÷ {guests} guest-nights = {pct}. If this goes above about a third, the sales assumption is probably too optimistic.
why.attachNa: Not sold per guest (e.g. EV charging), so this check doesn't apply.
why.subtotal: Quantity × cost per unit at the lodge.
why.kpiTotal: All {n} items added up, with the options currently chosen, delivered to the lodge. Imported items include shipping, {duty} customs duty and {vat} VAT, and everything includes the {remote} countryside premium unless switched off.
why.kpiNet: The {k} revenue-earning items bring in {gross} a year and cost {opex} a year to run ({scenario} scenario). Cost-only items add no income.
why.kpiPayback: {capex} invested in the revenue-earning items ÷ {net} net revenue a year. The {nc} spent on cost-only items isn't included — those are for comfort, safety and operations and don't pay back on their own.
why.split: Earns revenue: guests pay to use it. Partly earns: part of its cost is recovered from fees. Cost only: comfort, safety and operations — free for guests or used by the lodge itself.

assum.remoteNote: Transport UB → Dadal and countryside labour, on every item unless switched off
why.remote: Building or delivering anything in the countryside costs more than in Ulaanbaatar: trucking from UB to Dadal (about 550 km by road) and paying crews to work away from the city. A flat {pct} is added on top of the price and any import costs. It can be switched off for a single item — e.g. a quote that is already delivered and installed at the lodge.

fut.title: Further out — 2027–2029
fut.sub: Not part of this package and not counted anywhere — a heads-up on spending that may come later, so it is no surprise. Most of it depends on two things: whether we open a second lodge in Bulgan, and whether the paved road to Dadal is finished in 2028–2029. A paved road would make Dadal easy to reach all year and could bring many more guests, including in winter — so several items are about making the lodge fully usable in winter.
